summary: Autoscaler allocation rate limiter snap causes staggered GPU attach rejections and throughput sag
description:
Issue summary:
During a midday customer surge AtlasAI observed a sustained P99 and P50 throughput degradation on their Dedicated pool. This correlated to a sudden increase in allocation rejections from the global autoscaler rate limiter (metric: alloc_rate_limit_exceeded).

Impact:
- Intermittent 5xx attach errors for short-lived streams and high-fanout jobs for AtlasAI (dedicated tenant).
- Effective reserved GPU throughput dropped by ~28% over a 17-minute window, causing user-visible latency increases and retry storms.
- Fallbacks to cheaper model variants triggered, increasing token cost.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: atlas-dedicated-us-east-1 (reserved capacity)
- Region: us-east-1
- Models: gpt-medium-onnx (primary), redwood-compact-1 (fallback)
- Observed timeframe: 2026-03-13 12:10 - 12:27 UTC

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Simulate 3k/min short inference sessions (mean length 60 tokens) from many ephemeral workers, connection lifetime ~6s.
2) Rapid connect/disconnect pattern with a 100ms inter-request jitter.
3) Watch allocation_attempts, alloc_rate_limit_exceeded, allocator_attach_rejected counters.

Observed logs / errors:
- allocator: WARN alloc_rate_limit_exceeded tenant=atlasai pool=atlas-dedicated-us-east-1 burst=0
- allocator: ERROR attach_rejected tenant=atlasai reason=rate_limited attempts=3
- serving-runtime: 503 attach_failure context=short_stream
- autoscaler: debug insufficient_alloc_tokens pool=atlas-dedicated-us-east-1

Notes: customer reported the problem when running a bursty analytics sweep (many short-lived requests) combined with regular background keepalive probes. The allocation failure pattern showed a sawtooth where small cohorts became "silent" (failed to attach) then recovered, producing oscillatory throughput.
comments: 2026-03-13 12:35 UTC - Lena Park (Support): Initial report received from AtlasAI CS saying p99 rose and some requests returned 503s. Collected logs and initial graphs (links below). Escalating to SRE for autoscaler/allocator investigation.

2026-03-13 13:02 UTC - Marcus O'Neill (SRE): Confirmed alloc_rate_limit_exceeded spikes in tenant telemetry. Noted global alloc token bucket exhausted despite pool having free GPUs; hypothesis: global rate limiter configuration uses a shared burst bucket that doesn't account for dedicated pool reserved bursts.

2026-03-13 13:18 UTC - Engineering (autoscaler): Experimented with increasing allocation retry jitter + temporary per-pool burst override for AtlasAI. Initial mitigation reduced attach_rejected events by ~60% on canary pool.
2026-03-14 09:10 UTC - AtlasAI (Customer): Confirms visible latency and cost impact reduced after temporary change. Requests official postmortem and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence.
investigation: Timeline: 12:09 UTC - small burst of ephemeral streams begins; 12:10 UTC - alloc_rate_limit_exceeded metric spikes and attach_rejected counts climb; 12:27 UTC - burst ends, metrics recover.
Telemetry: alloc_attempts increased by 430% at peak for tenant atlasai while pool GPU utilization was at ~62% (i.e., GPUs available but alloc path was throttled).

Root hypothesis: a global token-bucket rate limiter that gates allocation attempts was configured with conservative burst size and shared across dedicated and hosted allocation traffic. Short-lived multi-connection fans exhausted the bucket causing attach rejections even though GPUs were free. This created silent cohorts and amplified noisy-neighbor effects as retries synchronized.
Correlation: The attach rejection pattern aligns with low-latency short streams (6-12s). Longer sessions did not see the same immediate failure mode but experienced queued delays.
Logs: sample allocator log snippets saved to S3: s3://redwood-support/SUP-864210/allocator_snippet_2026-03-13.log
Grafana dashboards referenced: Allocator -> rate_limiter_detail, Autoscaler -> pool_attach_failures, Serving -> s3://dashboards/atlasai-midday-spike
resolution: Immediate mitigations applied (2026-03-13 13:22 UTC): temporary per-pool burst override for atlas-dedicated-us-east-1 + increase allocation retry jitter to random(50-250ms). This reduced attach_rejected by ~60% and restored throughput close to baseline.

Root cause and permanent fix: autoscaler/global rate limiter will be updated to support per-pool token buckets and dynamic burst sizing based on reserved capacity. Implemented in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/789 and https://github.com/redwood-inference/allocator/pull/462. Engineering validated in staging and started gradual rollout 2026-03-14 04:00 UTC.

Follow-ups and runbook changes: added a dedicated runbook section for 'allocation-rate-limiter-snap' with playbook steps, alert thresholds (alloc_rate_limit_exceeded > 50/min for 3m triggers P1), and recommended per-customer burst configs for dedicated tenants. Confluence page updated.

Customer communication: Notified AtlasAI of temporary mitigation and planned permanent rollout. Offered a 2-week telemetry review window after full rollout. Finance notified for potential usage discrepancy caused by fallback invocations.

Monitoring: New alerts added and a weekly dashboard to surface short-stream-heavy tenants that could cause similar bursts. Post-deployment observation window: 72 hours with increased log sampling for allocation paths.
